newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares trundled to their fourth consecutive record high close, sweeping away fresh intra day highs as retail investors continued to clamour for stock.

"This market is still going on its own momentum. It's a train that no one can stop," said a dealer. "The dollar and bonds are OK, Wall Street's firm, people can't see any reason for the market to come down," he added.

The AEX share index closed 11.66 points higher at 918.85, back from a 919.84 trading high. The index last week put on over five percent from its low point of around 861 on Monday and dealers are saying the 1,000 barrier can fall soon.

Although the AEX has risen nearly 42 percent so far in 1997, investors are choosing to ignore reports from some brokers that prices are too high. The latest report came on Friday when U.S. bank JP Morgan said Dutch equities were overbought.
"You've got to go with the flow," said one dealer. "People have been telling us that the market was overbought since it crossed 700," he added.

"If anyone had told you in January that the AEX would be over 900 in July you'd have laughed at them. There's not much that can knock it back, unless we get a spate of U.S. (economic) figures that change the interest rate outlook," he added.
Dealers said the market could be susceptible to sporadic profit-taking and that a 30-40 point retracement could result from any statistic taken badly by investors.

"But unless you get a structural shift in the U.S. interest rate pattern -- series of figures that shows overheating -- or a string of bad Q2 company results, this market is still going to go up because there's so much liquidity," a dealer said.

Chart analysts remained bullish about the uptrend in the AEX but many were reticent about pin-pointing where overhead resistance might kick in as the bull market continues. "This is still a long market. Stick to your bullish scenario," said one.

"We expect some profit taking during the coming days, nevertheless the closing level of this week will probably be higher again...We still advise investors to use the possible slowdown to buy Dutch shares," said another chartist's note.

Corporate news was thin on the ground although KLM shares were perked up by news the Dutch company was buying out the stake it does not alreadyy hold in Air UK. KLM closed 2.50 guilders higher at 68.50.
Cyclicals gained on the perception they have lagged of late with Akzo up 5.80 guilders to 277.50 and DSM 4.50 guilders higher at 209.50. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
